children: Promoter Fosun Pharma has sold equity shares worth more than Rs 2,121 crore in Hyderabad-based Gland Pharma, a pharmaceutical company focused on generic injectables, through open-market transactions on September 4.

According to block deal data published by the National Stock Exchange, Fosun Pharma Industrial, a wholly owned subsidiary of Shanghai Fosun Pharmaceutical (Group) Co., sold 75.05 lakh shares, representing a 4.5 percent stake in Gland Pharma.
The shares, worth Rs 2,121.5 crore, were acquired by 11 institutional investors at Rs 2,826.6 per share.

Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund emerged as the biggest buyer, acquiring 27.93 lakh shares, or a 1.69 percent stake in Gland Pharma, for Rs 789.5 crore. It was followed by Axis Mutual Fund, which bought 13.57 lakh shares for Rs 383.6 crore, and ICICI Prudential AMC, which purchased 10.39 lakh shares for Rs 293.68 crore.

Other investors participating in the Gland Pharma block deal included Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, SBI Life Insurance Company, HDFC Standard Life Insurance, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, Societe Generale, Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance and Sundaram Mutual Fund.
Mirae Asset and ICICI Prudential AMC held 5.69 percent and 1.79 percent stakes in the pharmaceutical company, respectively, while Fosun Pharma’s stake stood at 51.77 percent as of June 2026.
Gland Pharma shares rose 0.84 percent to Rs 2,932.4 on September 4, their highest closing level since August 14, amid heavy trading volumes.
Former Tata Technologies CEO sells 0.51% stake

Patrick Raymon McGoldrick, former CEO and Managing Director of Tata Technologies, sold 21 lakh shares, representing a 0.51 percent stake in the engineering services company, for Rs 164.85 crore at Rs 785 per share.
McGoldrick retired as Managing Director and CEO of Tata Technologies in September 2014 after 20 years with the company.
ICICI Prudential AMC, Kotak Mahindra AMC, 360 ONE Asset Management and Carnelian Asset Management & Advisors bought the shares sold by McGoldrick.
Tata Technologies shares fell 0.63 percent to Rs 800 on September 4, extending their selling pressure through the week. The stock declined 4.12 percent during the week.
WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund buys Rs 123 crore worth of Nexus Select Trust units
Prashant Khemka’s WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund bought 74.95 lakh units of Nexus Select Trust from Blackstone-owned BREP Asia SG Forum Holding (NQ) for Rs 122.92 crore at Rs 164 per unit.

title: Block Deals: Fosun Pharma sells 4.5% stake in Gland Pharma for Rs 2,121 crore
